commits.message: Review (medium): a slot blended with itself is the slot, so prism/torn divide on named grounds; comments follow the per-cell rule (rich-joiners-9ntp.6pd)
Review (high): divider measured per seam cell; joinerNamed; torn divider; a real variant example (rich-joiners-9ntp.6pd)

JOINERS: the bundled joiner definitions by name (rich-joiners-9ntp.6pd)

One frozen table replaces POWERLINE_JOINER, CAPSULE_JOINER and PLAIN_JOINER:
powerline, prism, slant, backslant, flame, pixel, ice, bubble, capsule,
wrapper, metro, stitch, torn, plain — each a CellJoiner with its ASCII form.
metro's rail is the new strip.rail theme role. The rich-strip demo prints
the whole table, one joiner a row; its card grows to 30 rows.
Playground failure locator keeps the alert role; comment names every failure it shows (rich-playground-3cyp)

Playground e2e reads the playground's failure, not the card's run error (rich-playground-3cyp)

The fast-typing test types 250 x's, a program that throws a ReferenceError
once its debounced run finishes. The alert locator matched any [role=alert]
in the playground, the card's run failure included, so toHaveCount(0) passed
only when it checked before the run. It now names .rich-playground-failure,
the one element every use of it meant.

rich-dash drives frames from App's clock, not its own setInterval (rich-rich-dash-ds50) (#387)

* rich-dash drives frames from App's clock, not its own setInterval (rich-rich-dash-ds50)

The dashboard's widgets advance in the view, once per frame period of the
time App hands it, on a Clock that arrives in DashboardCapabilities. The
second timer, its Date.now reads and the try/catch that routed its errors
into app.fail are gone: a widget that throws now throws inside the frame,
which App already fails on. A suspended dashboard paints nothing and so
stands still, and a fake clock drives it (test/examples/rich-dash/app.test.ts).

TickContext had no reader in any widget and is deleted rather than
re-sourced.

* rich-dash counts frames with effects-feel's frameClock, now shared (rich-rich-dash-ds50)

Flooring absolute clock time into periods dropped a tick whenever a timer
frame landed a rounding error short of a period edge. A frame counter has
no edges to miss, and a repaint between frames is handed the same number.
